# WH-005 Inventory Adjustment Approvals

## 1. Purpose

### 1.1 Objective
This procedure states who may approve a change to the system inventory balance, so that write-ons and write-offs are controlled and traceable.

### 1.2 Scope
It applies to every manual change to on-hand quantity, including adjustments that follow a cycle count under WH-002, damage write-offs and scrap of returned goods under WH-004.

## 2. Approval Limits

### 2.1 Adjustment approval bands
The approver is set by the absolute value of the adjustment at standard cost, whether it increases or decreases stock.

| Adjustment value | Approver |
|---|---|
| Up to $500 | Warehouse Supervisor |
| $500 to $5,000 | Inventory Control Manager |
| Above $5,000 | Director of Operations plus Finance |

An adjustment of exactly $500 is approved by the Warehouse Supervisor, and an adjustment of exactly $5,000 by the Inventory Control Manager.

### 2.2 Director and Finance approval
An adjustment above $5,000 needs the approval of both the Director of Operations and a member of the Finance team. Both approvals must be recorded before the adjustment posts.

### 2.3 Multiple lines
Adjustments made for the same event, such as one damaged pallet, are added together to find the band. Splitting an event into several smaller adjustments is not permitted.

## 3. Reason Codes

### 3.1 Reason code is mandatory
Every adjustment must carry a reason code. The system rejects an adjustment with no code. The approver confirms that the code fits the facts before approving.

### 3.2 Standard reason codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| CNT | Cycle count variance |
| DMG | Damaged in warehouse |
| SCR | Scrapped |
| RCV | Receiving correction |
| RET | Returns correction |

### 3.3 Free text
A short free-text note explains the circumstances. Notes such as "adjust" or "fix" are not acceptable.

## 4. Process

### 4.1 Request
The requester enters the item, location, quantity change, reason code and note. Evidence such as the count sheet or photographs is attached.

### 4.2 Approval
The approver reviews and approves in the system. A requester cannot approve their own adjustment.

### 4.3 Posting and review
Approved adjustments post immediately. Inventory Control reviews the weekly list of adjustments and reports patterns to the Director of Operations.

## 5. Records

### 5.1 Retention
The request, evidence, approvals and posting are kept for seven years.

### 5.2 Month-end review
At month end Inventory Control prepares a summary of adjustments by reason code, zone and approver. Finance reviews the total value written off against the budget. Unusual patterns, such as many adjustments just below a band limit, are investigated by the Inventory Control Manager.

### 5.3 Responsibilities
Warehouse Supervisors approve only within their band and make sure evidence is attached. The Inventory Control Manager owns the reason code list and any changes to it. The Director of Operations owns this procedure and the approval limits in it.

### 5.4 Exceptions to the procedure
Urgent adjustments needed to release a customer shipment may be approved verbally by the approver for the band, but must be entered in the system within one working day with the reason code.

### 5.5 Rejected requests
A rejected adjustment is returned to the requester with the reason for rejection. The requester may resubmit with better evidence, or ask Inventory Control to arrange a recount under WH-002 before any change is made to the balance.
